podcast.title: Childhood Guitar Incident
podcast.body: When Johnny was six, his mother bought him a guitar, which, by the end of the day, he had broken over Dorsey's head in a fight. "By the end of the day both guitars had been broken over each other's heads."

podcast.title: Death in Boating Accident
podcast.body: Johnny Burnette died in a boating accident in 1964, cutting short his career before he could potentially regain the passion of his earlier recordings. "And sadly, we'll never know if he would regain that passion, as in 1964 he died in a voting accident."

podcast.title: Response to Hank Snow's Refusal
podcast.body: After Hank Snow refused to help the Rock and Roll Trio get onto the Grand Ole Opry, Johnny Burnette responded with two expletives and immediately turned around to drive back to Memphis, subsequently never playing a Hank Snow song live again. "Johnny Burnett replied with two words, the first of which would get this podcast bumped into the adult section in Apple Podcasts and the second of which was you and then they turned round and drove back to Memphis."

podcast.title: Sibling Rivalry with Dorsey
podcast.body: Johnny and his brother Dorsey were known for fighting violently and often, making their relationship notably turbulent among musical siblings. "But few pairs of brothers have fought as violently and as often as Johnny and Dorsey Bennett."

podcast.body: After moving separately to Los Angeles, Johnny and Dorsey Burnette ended up working together as songwriters, collaborating on material for other artists. "but when he and Lucy both moved separately to LA, they ended up working together as songwriters."

podcast.body: His string of hits as a solo artist was in a very different style from the Rock and Roll Trio records, lacking the raw power and passion of his earlier work. "had a string of hits that, like Dorsey's, were in a very different style from the rock and roll trio records."
